pawn.name: Pawn
pawn.movement: Moves forward 1 square (2 on its first move). Captures diagonally. Promotes on reaching the last rank.
pawn.utility: The backbone of the position. Controls the center, shields your pieces, and can become a queen.
tips: Don't create doubled or isolated pawns without a good reason.
A passed pawn in the endgame is often worth a win.
In the center (e4, d4, e5, d5), a pawn is at its strongest.

knight.name: Knight
knight.movement: Moves in an L-shape (2+1 squares). The only piece that can jump over others.
knight.utility: Excellent in closed positions. Creates devastating forks.
tips: Post it in the center (f3, c3, f6, c6) for maximum reach.
Avoid the edge: "a knight on the rim is dim".
Look for forks on king plus queen, or king plus rook.

bishop.name: Bishop
bishop.movement: Moves diagonally, any distance. Stays on the same color square for its whole life.
bishop.utility: King of open positions. The bishop pair is a lasting advantage.
tips: Hold on to both bishops for as long as you can.
An active bishop on a long diagonal (fianchetto) is very powerful.
Avoid blocking your bishops behind your own pawns.

rook.name: Rook
rook.movement: Moves in a straight line (ranks and files), any distance.
rook.utility: Queen of open files and the 7th rank. Decisive in the endgame.
tips: Double your rooks on an open file.
A rook on the 7th rank is often worth a pawn.
Activate your rooks by castling as early as possible.

queen.name: Queen
queen.movement: Combines the rook and bishop: ranks, files, and diagonals, any distance.
queen.utility: The most powerful piece. Use it to attack, not to defend on its own.
tips: Don't bring the queen out too early — it just gets chased around.
Coordinate it with another piece to threaten mate.
In the endgame, it can deliver mate on its own with just the king's help.

king.name: King
king.movement: Moves 1 square in any direction. Can never end a move in check.
king.utility: Keep it safe in the opening; it becomes an active piece in the endgame.
tips: Castle early to keep your king safe.
In the endgame, centralize your king — it's a strong piece (≈ 4 points).
Watch out for back-rank mate: leave your king an escape square in its pawn shield.

checkCheckmateStalemate.title: Check, checkmate, and stalemate
checkCheckmateStalemate.body: Check is an attack on the king — you must respond to it right away. Checkmate happens when there's no way out of check — the game ends there. Stalemate is a draw: the player to move has no legal move but isn't in check.

castling.title: Castling
castling.body: A special move that shifts the king 2 squares toward a rook, then places that rook on the other side of it. Conditions: neither the king nor that rook has moved, no pieces stand between them, the king isn't in check, and it doesn't pass through an attacked square.

enPassant.title: En passant
enPassant.body: If an opponent's pawn advances 2 squares and lands right beside yours, you can capture it as if it had only moved 1 square. You must do it immediately, or you lose the right.

promotion.title: Promotion
promotion.body: A pawn that reaches the last rank turns into a queen, rook, bishop, or knight — your choice. Usually a queen, but under-promoting to a knight can occasionally deliver a surprise mate.

gamePhases.title: The phases of a game
gamePhases.body: Opening (moves 1–15): develop your pieces, control the center, get your king to safety. Middlegame: build tactical and strategic plans. Endgame: activate your king and push a pawn to promotion.

pieceValues.title: The value of the pieces
pieceValues.body: Pawn = 1, Knight = 3, Bishop = 3, Rook = 5, Queen = 9, King = ∞. These values guide your trades, but how active a piece is matters just as much as its value on paper.

eloExplained.title: How your ELO rating works
eloExplained.body:
The ELO system measures your real skill level relative to your opponents. You start at 1000.

Each AI has a fixed rating:
• {{amateurLabel}}: 400  • {{debutantLabel}}: 800  • {{intermediaireLabel}}: 1200  • {{avanceLabel}}: 1600  • {{expertLabel}}: 2000

After each game, your ELO changes according to this formula:
ΔELO = K × (Score − Expected)

— K = 32 (volatility factor)
— Score: 1 (win), 0.5 (draw), 0 (loss)
— Expected: your win probability, calculated from the rating gap

In practice: beating a much stronger opponent earns you a lot; losing to a weaker one costs you dearly. A game where no move was played doesn't change your ELO.

scholar-mate.title: Scholar's Mate
scholar-mate.description: The fastest possible mate, in 4 moves. Perfect for catching an inexperienced opponent off guard.
steps: 2. f1 → c4 (eyes f7) , b8 → c6
3. d1 → h5 (double threat) , g8 → f6?? (bad defense)
4. h5 × f7# Checkmate!

italian-opening.title: Italian Game
italian-opening.description: One of the most classic openings. Central control and fast piece development.
steps: 2. g1 → f3 (attacks e5) , b8 → c6 (defends)
3. f1 → c4 (the Italian) , f8 → c5 (Giuoco Piano)
4. O-O — king safe

sicilian-defense.title: Sicilian Defense
sicilian-defense.description: The most popular response to 1.e4. Creates sharp, asymmetrical play.
steps: 1. e2 → e4 , c7 → c5 (the Sicilian)
4. f3 × d4 (knight to the center) , g8 → f6

back-rank.title: Back-Rank Mate
back-rank.description: Exploiting a king trapped on the back rank with no escape square.
steps: Spot a king with no escape square
Its own pawns block the way out (f7, g7, h7)
Attack the back rank with a rook or queen
Deliver mate on the 8th rank
boardStepLabels: The black king is trapped by f7, g7, h7

fork.title: The Fork
fork.description: Attacking two pieces at once with a single piece.
steps: Spot two enemy pieces that are poorly placed
Move a knight to attack both of them
Your opponent can only save one piece
Capture the piece left behind
boardStepLabels: Knight ready to pounce: king and rook both exposed
f3 → d4: a fork on king and rook!

pin.title: The Pin
pin.description: Immobilizing an enemy piece because moving it would expose a more valuable piece behind it.
steps: Line up your long-range piece with an enemy piece
Behind it: a more valuable piece (king or queen)
The pinned piece can no longer move
Capture it for free
boardStepLabels: The bishop lines up the queen and king on the same diagonal
b3 × d5: the queen was pinned — a free capture!

discovered-attack.title: Discovered Attack
discovered-attack.description: Moving one piece to unleash an attack from another piece hidden behind it.
steps: Spot a line of attack that your own piece is blocking
Move the blocking piece somewhere it creates a threat too
The discovered attack creates a double threat
Your opponent can't defend against both
boardStepLabels: f3 × e5: unleashes the bishop's attack on f7!

endgame-kp.title: King and Pawn Endgame
endgame-kp.description: Mastering the technique for promoting a pawn with the king's help.
steps: Advance your king in front of the pawn
The concept of opposition: facing the enemy king head-on
The king shelters the pawn's advance
Promote to a queen
boardStepLabels: White king in front of the pawn — the key to this endgame
The king advances and takes the opposition
The king escorts it in — the pawn is about to promote

castling-strategy.title: Castling Strategy
castling-strategy.description: When and how to castle to protect your king and activate your rook.
steps: Develop your knight and bishop first
Don't move your king or rooks unnecessarily
Kingside castling (O-O): the classic safe choice
Queenside castling (O-O-O): sets up an attack on the kingside
boardStepLabels: Knight developed — get ready to castle
Bishop developed — ready to castle kingside

smothered-mate.title: Smothered Mate
smothered-mate.description: An elegant mate where the knight delivers checkmate because the king is smothered by its own pieces.
steps: The enemy king is stuck in a corner
Its own pieces surround it
The knight leaps to f7 or h7
Unstoppable mate
boardStepLabels: Knight on f7: smothered mate! The king is trapped by its own rook and pawns.
